commit_conventions.observations: The project enforces nothing by tooling. Titles are short, imperative and lower case; 90 percent are at most 71 characters, and the few longer ones are old multi-topic commits, so staying within 72 is the safe reading even though no limit is kept. Three quarters use a prefix: conventional types (feat:, fix:, docs:, chore:) in recent history, component names (templates:, goreleaser:, actions:, Makefile:, run/qemu:) throughout. Use feat: for the platform support so it appears in the release changelog and goreleaser: for the release list, which the changelog filter hides. Bodies are rare; when present they are short bullet lists per component (PR 44) wrapped under about 75 columns, with a few longer lines. Issue references appear as "(close #19)" or "fix #65" in titles. Signed-off-by is on 94 of 100 commits: all but one of those written by the maintainer, and the dependabot ones; the six without it are five merged external commits and one early maintainer commit, so the trailer is the house style but was not enforced on contributors. Keep it on the commits of this contribution. What the maintainer does ask external contributors for is a verified (GPG or SSH) signature and one squashed, rebased commit per pull request, while his own pull requests carry up to three commits, one per logical change. For this contribution two commits fit the history (feat: platform support with templates, qemu and docs; goreleaser: release architectures), and a single squashed commit is equally acceptable; a third is tolerated only for an isolated, unrelated test fix.

dependency_graph.assessment: The tool succeeded, but the graph has no node for d2vm under any identity (project name, repository URL, package name, identity name, upstream repository): this is missing data, not an empty dependency set, and no direct, transitive or reverse edge of d2vm can be taken from the graph. The graph holds Ubuntu resolute packages for amd64, arm64 and riscv64, so it was used for what it can answer: the host tools d2vm calls at run time (parted, kpartx, e2fsprogs, dosfstools, cryptsetup, qemu-utils, util-linux, udev, docker.io) and Go 1.25 all have riscv64 binaries; the Ubuntu guest packages the riscv64 template path installs (linux-image-virtual, grub-efi-riscv64-bin) exist for riscv64; extlinux and grub-pc-bin are amd64 only, which the code already reflects by refusing syslinux and grub-bios off x86; qemu-system-riscv and the qemu-efi-riscv64 firmware exist on amd64 hosts. cryptsetup-initramfs shows no riscv64 binding in the query result; whether that is an architecture-all package recorded only under two architectures or a real gap is not decided by the graph, and the CI luks cases on riscv64 (ubuntu:24.04, debian:13) passed at the development head. linux-image-riscv64 is a Debian package and is outside this Ubuntu-only graph; it was verified by the passing debian:13 riscv64 e2e job instead. Compared with the checkout: go.mod (go 1.25) lists 17 direct and 34 indirect modules, all pure Go (no cgo import, no assembly file, only a windows build tag pair in pkg/docker), and CGO_ENABLED=0 GOARCH=riscv64 go build ./cmd/d2vm at 7184ff1 produced a static RISC-V ELF in this run. Build-time: Go modules and, through go generate, the sparsecat helper built for linux amd64 and arm64 only (Hetzner upload path). Run-time: the host tools above and docker. Test-time: docker, qemu-system, OVMF, distribution base images. Reverse dependencies are unknown to the graph; pkg.go.dev shows d2vm as an application module.

project.riscv64_toolchain: Go: linux/riscv64 is a first-class Go port (rv64g, RVA20U64 mandatory since Go 1.23 per go.dev/wiki/MinimumRequirements; go.dev/dl ships linux-riscv64 archives); the module needs go 1.25, has no cgo or assembly and cross-compiled to a static RISC-V ELF at 7184ff1 in this run (Go 1.26.11 host). windows/riscv64 and darwin/riscv64 are not Go ports (go tool dist list) and goreleaser v1.10.1 skips them. golang:1.25 and ubuntu:20.04, 22.04, 24.04 have linux/riscv64 manifests; docker:dind does not. Guest tooling: grub-efi-riscv64-bin and riscv64 kernels exist for Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 (both booted in CI at the development head) and in Ubuntu resolute (project graph); Ubuntu 22.04 has a riscv64 base image but was not exercised; edk2 firmware for the QEMU virt machine is packaged as qemu-efi-riscv64; tonistiigi/binfmt provides riscv64 user emulation. syslinux, extlinux and grub-pc are x86 only.

proposal.architecture_precedent: Shared host without an architecture axis: every Linux job runs on one ubuntu-latest amd64 runner with docker/setup-qemu-action and apt qemu-system; there is no architecture list in any workflow and no native per-architecture runner row. arm64 (PR 44) is the precedent and has no CI row at all: its support consists of the goarch entry in .goreleaser.yaml, the linux/arm64 platform case restricted to grub-efi, and template package selection. Recommendation, as steered by the owner: add riscv64 to the same lists (goarch, platform switches, template package selection) and add no CI row, neither a shared-host QEMU row nor an ubuntu-24.04-riscv runner row.
proposal.build_and_dependencies: Go modules, go 1.25, CGO_ENABLED=0, 17 direct and 34 indirect pure Go modules; linux/riscv64 cross-build verified at 7184ff1. Run-time host tools (docker, parted, kpartx, e2fsprogs, dosfstools, cryptsetup, qemu-utils) exist for riscv64 in Ubuntu (project graph, suite resolute). Guest side for --platform linux/riscv64: ubuntu:24.04 (linux-image-virtual, grub-efi-riscv64-bin) and debian:13 (linux-image-riscv64, grub-efi-riscv64-bin) have riscv64 base images and packages and booted in CI at the development head; ubuntu:22.04 has a riscv64 base image but was not exercised; debian:12, debian:11, rockylinux:9, almalinux:10, centos:8 and kali have no riscv64 base image; Alpine has one but its template path is not enabled. Not available for riscv64: docker:dind (so no riscv64 d2vm image), extlinux and grub-pc (x86 only, already refused by the code). No Python dependency exists, so no PyPI or RISE index setting applies.

proposal.rationale: Develop. The requested upstream luhenry/d2vm (a fork of linka-cloud/d2vm at the same main commit 7184ff1) is a pure Go tool (CGO disabled, no assembly) that already cross-compiles to linux/riscv64, but the binary is unusable there: version.go makes linux/riscv64 its default platform, and builder.go and cmd/d2vm/flags.go reject every platform except linux/amd64 and linux/arm64; pkg/qemu and d2vm run qemu have no riscv64 machine; the Debian and Ubuntu templates pick amd64 or arm64 package names; .goreleaser.yaml releases amd64 and arm64 only. A bounded patch that fixes this exists on development PR 1 (head 6578833) and follows the accepted arm64 precedent (linka-cloud PR 44): linux/riscv64 as a platform restricted to grub-efi, dpkg-architecture based package names in the Debian and Ubuntu templates, the riscv64 virt machine with edk2 on pflash in pkg/qemu, riscv64 in the goreleaser goarch list, README and regenerated CLI reference. It is validated: both CI runs on that head converted and booted ubuntu:24.04 and debian:13 for linux/riscv64, all amd64 e2e rows stayed green and the Build job built the goreleaser snapshot with riscv64. The owner's review then set the shape of the contribution, and this plan follows it: (1) no riscv64 CI testing, because arm64 has none and everything is built and tested on x86 only, so .github/workflows/ci.yaml returns to base; (2) no riscv64 cross-testing in e2e/e2e_test.go, so that file and the Makefile E2E_PLATFORM pass-through return to base; (3) .goreleaser.yaml states the excluded combinations with an ignore list for windows/riscv64 and darwin/riscv64 (goreleaser v1.10.1 already skips them silently, verified in its source, so the release output is unchanged). The remaining series is the platform support, the release list and the documentation, which is exactly what PR 44 did for arm64. Class architecture_correctness: the change adds a missing architecture case to source switches and templates so the tool behaves correctly on and for riscv64. Known open point: the CI job Test Templates (debian) failed in both runs and its log could not be read in this run. The Debian template renders identically on amd64 at head and base and the same template passed for Kali, so a regression is not evident, but the cause is not verified; the developer must read the job log first and may touch config_test.go or the workflow only if the log proves a failure that also exists on base. Nothing upstream objects to riscv64; there is no prior riscv64 work, no ecosystem report and no project-graph node.

Per the owner's steering the riscv64 contribution therefore adds no CI row, neither on the shared host nor on a native ubuntu-24.04-riscv runner, and returns ci.yaml, e2e/e2e_test.go and the Makefile to base. Fork guards: none; publishing steps are gated by tag or main ref and need secrets, so on a fork pull request all test and build jobs run and the release jobs are skipped. State of the development head: functionally validated. Both runs converted and booted ubuntu:24.04 and debian:13 for linux/riscv64 under emulation, all amd64 e2e rows passed, and the Build job proved goreleaser v1.10.1 accepts goarch riscv64. That evidence stays valid for the series after the test code is removed, because the product code does not change. Open failure: Test Templates (debian) failed in both runs in step Run tests. Inference only: the failure is more likely a base or environment problem than a regression of the series (candidates: the end-of-life debian:11 image, runner disk space or registry limits while 32 Debian variants build in parallel, the job took longer than the last passing upstream run). The developer must read the log of job 138436926310 before changing anything, and must also get the Ubuntu, CentOS, Rocky and Alma template jobs to run to completion, since fail-fast cancelled them and the changed Ubuntu template has no completed template-test result yet. goreleaser: verified in source that v1.10.1 skips windows/riscv64 and darwin/riscv64, and go tool dist list has only linux/riscv64 and openbsd/riscv64. Consequence to state in the contribution: on riscv64 d2vm must run natively as root, because the automatic re-execution inside the linkacloud/d2vm image (used when not root or not on Linux) has no riscv64 image, exactly as on arm64. luhenry/d2vm itself releases nothing.

data.summary: d2vm (Go module go.linka.cloud/d2vm) converts Docker images into bootable VM disk images. The requested upstream luhenry/d2vm is a fork of linka-cloud/d2vm; both mains are at 7184ff1 and luhenry/d2vm has no issues, pull requests, tags or Actions runs of its own, so upstream history was researched in linka-cloud/d2vm (42 issues, 51 pull requests, all states). Base supports linux/amd64 and, since linka-cloud PR 44, linux/arm64 with grub-efi only; nothing upstream mentions RISC-V. This is a plan refresh for development PR riseproject-upstreaming/d2vm#1 at head 6578833, whose repair budget was exhausted. That head already adds linux/riscv64 as an EFI-only platform (builder.go, cmd/d2vm/flags.go, pkg/qemu, cmd/d2vm/run/qemu.go, Debian and Ubuntu templates, goreleaser goarch, README and CLI reference) and both CI runs on it booted ubuntu:24.04 and debian:13 riscv64 images end to end. The repository owner then requested changes in three review comments: drop the riscv64 CI rows, drop the riscv64 cross-testing in e2e/e2e_test.go because not even arm64 has any, and exclude the windows and darwin riscv64 combinations in .goreleaser.yaml. Decision: develop, class architecture_correctness. The series keeps the platform support, release list and documentation, returns .github/workflows/ci.yaml, e2e/e2e_test.go and the Makefile to their base content, and makes the goreleaser exclusion explicit. One CI job, Test Templates (debian), failed in both runs; its log could not be read with the read-only tooling of this run, the rendered Debian template is equivalent to base on amd64, and the cause is recorded as undetermined with the checks the developer must make first. No ecosystem report and no project-graph node exist for d2vm. The riscv64-draft branch of luhenry/d2vm was not read, as the tracking issue requires.
